chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Amyera, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one from the believers who is afflicted with an affliction, so he is patient upon it, there would be for him the like of the Recompense of a thousand martyrs'.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a patient believer who endures hardship?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the immense spiritual merit of sabr during personal trials. The comparison to a thousand martyrs underscores that steadfast endurance in suffering carries a weight comparable to the ultimate sacrifice of jihad, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology and jurisprudence. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the theological value of passive endurance alongside active struggle in the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Amyera, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one from the Believers who is afflicted with an affliction, so he is patient upon it, there would be for him the like of the Recompense of a thousand martyrs’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu Hamza al-Thumali who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whoever among the believers exercises patience at the time of suffering hardship he will have a reward equal to the reward of a thousand martyrs.’”
